indian.headline: Indian markets close higher on metal and pharma strength despite lingering oil concerns.
indian.lead: Indian markets close higher on metal and pharma strength despite lingering oil concerns.
indian.brief: Sensex gained 0.66% and Nifty 50 rose 0.68%, with Bank Nifty up just 0.15%, as metal stocks surged 2.2% and pharma climbed 1.8%.
why: Metal sector rallied 2.2%, the day's strongest performer, lifting index heavyweights and offsetting week-long losses from oil price spikes.
Pharma gained 1.8% as investors rotated into defensive sectors amid persistent West Asia tensions and crude oil concerns that had weighed on markets last week.
Banking showed minimal movement at +0.1%, reflecting caution in financial stocks despite the broader index recovery, capping upside momentum.

Reliance's Jio Platforms IPO allotment on 26 October — with unprecedented 22.19x subscription — drew retail money into new offerings, creating a seesaw between secondary market recovery and capital diversion to the ₹5 trillion IPO pipeline.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities staged a modest recovery on 26 October after a weak week, with the Sensex gaining 0.66% and Nifty 50 rising 0.68%. The turnaround was driven by a sharp 2.2% surge in metal stocks — the day's standout winner — paired with pharma's 1.8% gain as investors sought shelter from oil-linked volatility. However, the rally remained muted: Bank Nifty edged up just 0.15%, and most other sectors gained under 1%, signalling lingering caution.

The undercurrent tells a complex story. While indices clawed back losses, sentiment remained fractured by last week's 2.4% Nifty plunge on crude oil strength and West Asia tensions. Simultaneously, Reliance's Jio Platforms IPO — which finalised allotment today after attracting 1.39 crore applications and ₹7.4 lakh crore in bids — is pulling retail capital toward new offerings rather than existing stocks. Analysts warn that a ₹5 trillion IPO pipeline is redirecting money away from the secondary market into IPOs, leaving the broader rally shallow and vulnerable to the next global or oil-price shock.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: Oil surge and West Asia tensions persist; Fed focus remains. Last week Nifty fell 2.4%.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: No fresh data on direct FII moves; capital is rotating toward ₹5 trillion IPO pipeline instead.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: Oil price surge weighed on markets last week; remains a key headwind for sentiment today.

indian.watch: Jio Platforms listing price and PSU Q2 earnings (Coal India, BEL, IGL) this week; oil prices and Fed moves.

us.headline: US markets closed lower as earnings season looms and investor confidence weakens.
us.lead: US markets closed lower as earnings season looms and investor confidence weakens.
us.brief: S&P 500 fell 0.52%, Nasdaq dropped 0.21%, and Dow declined 1.23%, with Energy the sole gainer at +2.6%.
why: More than one-third of S&P 500 companies report earnings this week, raising uncertainty and prompting profit-taking ahead of results.
Tech and Financials sectors fell (0.5% and -1.3%) despite broad market weakness, signaling selective sector rotation into defensive plays.
Healthcare declined 1.1%, suggesting investors are cautious on growth-dependent sectors while watching macro risks unfold.
us.narrative:
US stock markets retreated on October 26 as the earnings season kicked into high gear. With over one-third of the S&P 500's largest companies about to report quarterly results, traders grew cautious. The Dow bore the brunt of selling, dropping 1.23%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq fell more modestly at 0.52% and 0.21% respectively. Healthcare and Financials stocks led the decline, shedding 1.1% and 1.3%, though Energy bucked the trend with a 2.6% gain.

Investor confidence is cracking ahead of earnings announcements, a sign that markets are pricing in softer corporate performance. In India, IT stocks grabbed attention as five major companies announced dividend payouts this week, with L&T Technology Services leading at ₹20 per share. Infosys, a bellwether IT firm, saw shares crash 4% after disappointing Q2 results, reflecting broader caution in the sector. Globally, food-tech startup Wonder is gearing up for a potential IPO, while SoftBank committed $50 billion to Malaysia's AI infrastructure push, showing tech investors remain active despite near-term market weakness.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: Only sector gainers today; safe-haven play

us.watch: Watch earnings results this week and how companies guide forward—weak outlooks could extend today's selloff.
